title: DC motor
lines: The walking skeleton: one physical model, built twice, as iconic components and as a bond graph.
R = 2 ohm, k_t = 0.05 N·m/A, a 12 V supply step at t = 0.01 s.
The run: rotor speed rises to a steady state; both forms agree.

title: Series RLC, twice
lines: One model, two independent subsystems: an iconic circuit and the same circuit as a pure bond graph.
Both are driven by a 1 V step.
The run: the capacitor voltage rings and settles; the two forms overlap.

title: Bouncing ball
lines: A single equation block from the project library with a continuous event.
Released from rest at h = 1 m; each impact reverses the velocity and loses 20 % of the speed.
The run: height curve with a kink at every bounce.

title: Quarter-car suspension
lines: Bond graph: 300 kg sprung mass, 40 kg unsprung mass, a one-sided tyre and a ±0.08 m hard stop.
A table-driven road with a 5 cm plateau bump at t = 0.5 s.
The run: 4 s of body and wheel motion over the bump.

title: Drivetrain
lines: Motor, gearbox and a flexible rod between two inertias, as an iconic model and as a pure bond graph.
A 12 V step at t = 0.01 s, a 0.5 N·m load step at t = 1 s.
The run: 2 s; both forms give the same numbers.

title: Drivetrain with LQG
lines: A bond-graph plant under a 1 ms discrete LQG firmware: LQR with integral action plus a Kalman filter.
The filter reconstructs the load speed from the motor encoder alone.
The run: a 10 rad/s reference step at 0.1 s, a −0.5 N·m load step at 1 s.

title: Position control of a compliant drivetrain
lines: The same drivetrain with a shaft 40x softer: a 3.9 Hz torsional mode.
A 1 rad step of the load wheel, then a load-torque step.
A textbook PID overshoots by 104 % and rings at 3.8 Hz. Trajectory, Kalman filter on both encoders and LQR with integral action: 0.02 % overshoot, settling in 0.66 s.

title: Hydraulic servo
lines: A 100 bar supply and a 1 bar tank feed a 4/3 spool valve built from four variable orifices.
The valve drives a cylinder with a 50 kg mass; a 1 ms discrete PID closes the position loop.
The run: the piston follows its position command.

title: Industrial servo drive
lines: A PMSM drive: bond-graph dq plant, sampled cascaded current, speed and position firmware, and an inverter.
Five fidelity variants; the first is the baseline with an averaged inverter and a rigid inertia.
The run: the speed response of the cascaded loops.

title: Cart-pole balancer
lines: A pure bond-graph cart with a rod and tip mass, balanced by a 1 ms discrete LQR.
It starts with a 0.1 rad tilt and follows a 0.2 m cart-position step at t = 1.5 s.
The run: the pole is stabilised and the cart moves.

title: Planar multibond pendulum
lines: A rigid link on a compliant-pivot planar revolute joint, built from Power{Planar} multibonds.
Shown with the two-stroke bond convention end to end.
The run: a 10 s swing; the energy drift stays at numerical noise.

title: Planar 2-link arm
lines: Two rigid links and a payload on compliant pivots, built from planar multibond composites.
A 1 ms PD controller with gravity feedforward drives both joints.
The run: the joints move to their targets.

title: Planar links vs. a toolbox
lines: The 1-, 2- and 3-link planar arms, built side by side from planar bond-graph elements.
CSV input sources drive them with reference trajectories.
The run: the arms follow the reference, compared with a robotics-toolbox model.

title: Reaction-wheel cube, 1D
lines: A 0.12 m cube on one edge, balanced by a DC motor spinning a wheel inside it.
A 2 ms discrete LQR sets the motor voltage, clamped to ±12 V.
The run: starting 0.05 rad off upright, the cube is held up.

title: Planar reaction-wheel balancer
lines: An inverted planar body on a compliant pivot with a reaction wheel on its axis.
A 1 ms PD on the body angle commands the wheel torque.
The run: the wheel spins up while the body stays upright.

title: Double pendulum, fixed pivot
lines: A planar double pendulum; a gearmotor drives the first joint only.
Hanging at rest, then a trajectory-optimised swing-up tracked by a time-varying LQR.
The run: swing-up, catch, balance, then a force pulse and the recovery.

title: Triple pendulum, fixed pivot
lines: A planar triple pendulum; a gearmotor drives the first joint, the other two are passive.
Swing-up along a trajectory-optimised feed-forward, tracked by a time-varying LQR.
The run: swing-up, catch, balance, recovery.

title: Double pendulum on a cart
lines: A cart on a ±0.40 m rail, driven through a gearbox and a belt; both pendulum joints are passive.
Everything starts hanging at rest; swing-up, LQR catch, then a force pulse on the tip.
The run: swing-up, catch, balance, recovery.

title: Triple pendulum on a cart
lines: The double-pendulum cart rig with a third link, on the same ±0.40 m belt-driven rail.
Swing-up from hanging, catch with an LQR, balance, then a force pulse on the tip link.
The run: swing-up, catch, balance, recovery.

title: Rotary double pendulum
lines: A Quanser-style rotary arm (70:1 gearbox, ±10 V) with a two-link pendulum, as a spatial multibond.
Swing-up at 1 s, catch at 5.02 s, a 0.35 N pulse at 8.5 s.
The run: 12 s from hanging to balance and recovery.

title: Rotary triple pendulum
lines: The rotary arm with a three-link chain (70:1 gearbox, ±15 V), a spatial multibond bond graph.
Swing-up at 1 s, LQR catch at about 5 s, a 0.1 N pulse at 8.5 s.
The run: 12 s from hanging to balance and recovery.

title: Six-axis arm
lines: A UR5-like serial arm on spatial multibonds; every joint bond is a three-stroke bundle.
A 1 ms PD controller with gravity feedforward.
The run: the arm moves from a home pose to a target pose.

title: Four-wheel pyramid on a spherical pivot
lines: A rigid body on a compliant spherical pivot carrying four reaction wheels in a pyramid.
Gyroscopic coupling is physical: every wheel is a real rigid body on a revolute joint.
The run: gravity off, so the total angular momentum about the pivot stays constant.

title: Cube on a corner
lines: A 0.15 m cube on one corner, body diagonal vertical, starting 2° off, with three reaction wheels.
A 2 ms discrete LQR sets the three motor voltages, clamped to ±12 V.
The run: the three wheels hold the cube balanced.

title: Cube tipping on four wheels
lines: A free 0.2 m cube with four reaction wheels in a pyramid on a compliant ground.
A scripted torque profile tips it from a face to an edge (45°) to a corner (54.74°).
The run: the contact phases are emergent, nothing is switched by hand.

title: Tetrahedron with wheels
lines: A regular tetrahedron (edge 0.25 m) with a reaction wheel on every face, lying on a ground plane.
A scripted torque profile spins the wheels.
The run: the body tips from a face to an edge to a single vertex.

title: Quadcopter
lines: A 1.35 kg, 450 mm X quadcopter with motor and propeller chains and a PX4-style cascaded flight controller.
The plant stands on four compliant contact legs.
The run: the 18 s mission: take-off to 1 m, a 2 m x 2 m square with a 90° yaw turn, landing.

title: Aerial manipulator
lines: A 2.1 kg hexarotor with a servo-driven tube, a rubber shock mount and a three-wheel end-effector.
Free flight, wall approach, engage at 5.08 s, a contact-controlled climb along the wall, disengage.
The run: the 34 s scenario with a gain-scheduled LQR contact controller.
